title: Send a refund only when every step agrees, and say which step refused

blocks.text: The support desk refunds orders through `Refunds.refund(orderId, cents)`. Three steps can refuse: the order store doesn't know the order, the amount is more than what is left to refund (or isn't positive), or the bank refuses the payment. All three are everyday outcomes, and the desk's screen shows the reason to the agent.
Two incidents last month: a refund larger than the order went to the bank anyway, and an agent saw "refund failed" for an order id with a typo in it, with no hint what was wrong.

Finish `refund` in `src/main/java/practice/Refunds.java`. The order store and the gateway already answer with a `Result`, and `refundable(order, cents)` checks the amount. When you're done, money reaches the gateway only when the order exists and the amount is allowed, and every refusal comes back as an `Err` that the desk can show as it is. About twelve lines in total.
The tests use their own orders, amounts and gateway answers.

cases.says: an allowed amount on a known order is sent once and comes back as Ok with the gateway's reference
an unknown order comes back as Err and the gateway is never called
an amount the check refuses is never sent to the gateway
an amount above what is left is returned as an Err with the check's reason, not thrown
an Err carries the reason of the step that refused: the order store's or the bank's

origin.section: A Sealed Result Makes an Expected Failure a Value the Caller Has to Match

concepts: With a sealed Result each step returns an expected failure as a value, and every layer must pass it on by hand, keeping its reason and stopping before the next step.
